Definition: of Hebrew origin (compare H2285); Agabus, an Israelite:--Agabus.
BiblicalUsage: Agabus was a prophet from Jerusalem who came to Antioch and foretold a great famine throughout the world — which came to pass in the days of Claudius — and who years later bound Paul's girdle around his own hands and feet, foretelling that the Jews at Jerusalem would bind its owner and deliver him to the Gentiles. Twice he spoke, and twice the word came true.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Agabus shows what a true prophet looks like: he speaks plainly, his words come to pass, and his hardest word is the one that tells a friend he will suffer. Paul listened, thanked him, and went to Jerusalem anyway — and that is what faithfulness looks like on both sides.
